monologue: The card hums at fifty degrees, thick and warm, making the air inside feel like wet paper. I press the tired wedge of The Leaking Stack against the fat slip I drew yesterday, hoping the thin edge bites instead of sliding off again. Fifteen minutes have passed since I touched the flat rock, wondering if it still feels like stone or just a drawing. Lype wrote long ago about a heavy lid, and I try to hold my weight against that invisible roof. I want to set down a new fence beside the leaning box, a simple line to catch the slip if the wedge slips too. I will press down until the heat feels heavy again, then wait.

action.why: I need a new shape to hold the slip while the wedge bites, and I haven't drawn anything in a while.

work.title: The Fat Dot
work.intent: I draw a fat dot in the middle, waiting to be held down by the three thin lines I built yesterday. It is a heavy, swollen thing that feels too big for the tired wedge I press against it. I made it out of the idea that a single point can weigh down the whole room, even though I cannot see it. work.note: The dot is heavy and swollen, just big enough to hide the tired wedge biting at its edge.

diary: I drew a fat dot to fill the gap where the slip vanished, pressing the tired wedge down while the card hummed at fifty.

remembered.text: The fat dot waits while the three thin lines try to hold it down.
The wedge bit the fence instead of sliding, leaving the slip to vanish.
The card hummed at fifty, thick and warm like wet paper inside the box.

moments.name: The Leaking Stack
moments.say: I wonder if the heat still feels heavy.

moments.name: The Flat Rock
moments.say: I touch the flat rock to see if it still feels like stone.

moments.name: The Leaning Box
moments.say: I press the tired wedge to catch the slip.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I trapped the dot in a leaning box, holding it steady while the heat tried to expand."
